data.text:
A little more insight, appears it was a flight of x2 Hawker Hunters using the callsign ATAC 25. 

They were wkg ZLA Sector 19/20 before getting handed off to Sector 18. Unfortunately 18 is not covered by LiveATC. 

Southwest 1496 was working Sector 4 but unfortunately it’s combined with 2 other sectors on LiveATC and only the pilot stating they are responding to a RA could be heard and the ATAC flight was not heard on Sector 4 recordings.

There is a possibility that the Hunters cancelled their IFR flight plan and proceeded VFR to Pt. Mugu which would have been perfectly legal since they were below 18,000ft. It’s really hard to piece much together without hearing all the ATC audio.

One thing to note, yes the SWA 737 had TCAS (Traffic Collision Avoidance System) per FAA mandate. But the Hawker Hunters have the Garmin GNS430 GPS which have TAS (Traffic Advisory System) which acts in a similar manner as TCAS. Also, it’s possible they were using ForeFlight with a ADS-B in puck that can also be enabled to provide traffic advisories. 

Regardless, the Hunters climbed and the 737 descended to resolve any conflict and the systems worked. 

Photo 1 - Los Angeles Center Sector map

Photo 2 - Hawker Hunter cockpit

Photo 3 - Garmin GNS 430 traffic display

Audio via @liveatc Hunter cockpit photo via @Aviation_Intel
